features.title: Copy button shows no label when there is room for one
features.summary: The Copy button dropped its word whenever `compact` was true, and that flag was computed from the stored pane-width setting rather than the space available: before settings load it used the 286 px default, so a wider pane painted icon-only and grew the word a moment later, and it also ignored how many action buttons shared the row. The decision is now a CSS container query on the action row itself: the word shows whenever the row is wide enough for it, evaluated at first paint with no state to wait for. The threshold is set from the worst case - a row of four action buttons beside the chevron - so nothing is dropped while it still fits.

features.title: Hide the bulk Markdown button when no text clip is selected
features.summary: The bulk bar's Markdown button now appears only when the selection contains at least one text clip, since only text clips have anything to write; the matching 'Export N as Markdown' entry in the right-click menu follows the same rule so the two cannot disagree. Selecting a run of screenshots no longer offers an action that quietly does nothing.

features.title: Colour picker shows both hex and RGB
features.summary: Implemented: the magnifier footer now prints the hex on one row and the RGB triple on the next, from fixed origins so the readout cannot shift, with the footer height added to the popup. The hex is upper case like the rest of the UI while the copied payload stays lower case. Three tests cover the formatting and prove no sample can outgrow the reserved space.

features.title: Thumbnail view shows mixed-case hex
features.summary: Fixed: the card caption printed the stored payload, so a colour read #6D8CFF in the swatch and #6d8cff underneath it. It now goes through displayHex, the helper the swatch, the rows and the properties pane already used, so the payload keeps its original casing.

features.title: Screenshot buttons at the top of the left sidebar
features.summary: Implemented: a capture toolbar sits at the top of the left sidebar, in the strip under the title bar above the first section header, sharing it with the collapse chevron. The eyedropper comes first, then region, window, full screen and scroll, with a hairline after the eyedropper. Icon-only because the sidebar is 186 px wide, with tooltips and accessible names; the row takes the place of the old top padding rather than adding height. The buttons are plain and independent of the title-bar split button, so a click does not change the remembered capture type. In the collapsed rail the five buttons stack as a vertical column over the expand target, with an opaque backing so clicks between the icons do not expand the sidebar.

features.title: Option to hide the title bar colour and capture icons
features.summary: Implemented: a `title_bar_capture` boolean defaults to on, so a fresh install looks exactly as before. Turning it off removes the eyedropper, the split capture button and the dividers that separated the group, leaving the settings button and the window controls in place with no leftover gap. It does not touch the sidebar capture strip, the capture hotkeys or the remembered capture mode.

features.title: Colour scheme row under a previewed image
features.summary: Implemented: previewing an image shows its colour scheme as a row at the bottom of the preview, each swatch with its hex, plus an eyedropper that samples a colour from the image itself (not the whole screen) and appends it to the clip's scheme, and a Save colour palette button beside the row that reuses the existing palette-archive action. Adding is idempotent: a colour already in the scheme is not duplicated. The store gained an add-colour path with tests for deduplication and persistence.

features.title: Copy Color Scheme button in an archive of colour clips
features.summary: Implemented: a toolbar appears above the list when the current view holds at least two colour clips, with a Copy Color Scheme button that copies every hex one per line, in on-screen list order, de-duplicated keeping the first occurrence, upper-cased to match the rest of the UI, with no trailing blank line. The transformation is a small pure module with tests.

features.title: Tag colours applied in list and card views
features.summary: Implemented: one shared TagChip now renders tags in the rows, the card grid and the properties pane, so a tag's stored colour is used everywhere it is read. The chip surface is an opaque tint of the tag colour and the ink is chosen from that surface's luminance past the WCAG cutoff, so pale and deep tags stay readable on both themes; sizes and padding are unchanged. Anything unparseable falls back to the neutral chip. Cards also show their tags now.

features.title: Remove the wizard's Try Now button
features.summary: Finished: Try Now is gone and Finish is the single way out of the wizard, taking the primary position alone instead of leaving a gap. It ends in exactly the state Try Now used to produce. Nothing references the removed button.

features.title: Print Screen opens CopyPaste
features.summary: Implemented: Print Screen runs the default capture type once the option is on. The key belongs to the Snipping Tool until its per-user handler is switched off, so turning the option on records what Windows had, writes 0, and registers the key; turning it off releases the key first and then writes the original value back. A failed registration gives the key straight back, and Print Screen cannot also be bound to a capture action. The wizard's first page offers the toggle and a horizontal icon radio group for Screen, Window or Selection, and the same default type is what the header split button offers.

features.title: A shortcut for every capture type and the colour picker
features.summary: Implemented: region, window, full screen, scroll and the colour picker each have an optional global shortcut, stored in settings, sanitised with the same rule as the existing hotkeys, and shown as a column of five rows in Settings with the recorder the current hotkey field uses. Empty means no shortcut and registers nothing. A combination Windows refuses because another application owns it is reported back and the previous shortcut stays active.

features.title: Quick preview renders Markdown
features.summary: Implemented: a Markdown clip opens rendered — headings, emphasis, strikethrough, inline and fenced code, both list kinds, quotes, rules and links — with a footer toggle back to the source. The renderer produces React elements rather than an HTML string, so no clip can inject markup; a link target that is not http(s) or mailto keeps its source text instead of becoming clickable.

features.title: Quick preview window is resizable
features.summary: Implemented: a grip in the bottom-right corner drags the dialog between a usable minimum and the space actually available, and the footer keeps clear of it. The size lives in the overlay's own state, so closing the preview resets it and the next one opens at the default size.

features.title: Quick Preview item in the clip context menu
features.summary: Implemented: Quick preview in the clip context menu does what Space does, on the clip that was right-clicked even when it was not the selected one, and refuses a file list for the same reason Space does.

features.title: Show Properties item in the clip context menu
features.summary: Implemented: Show properties selects the clip and expands the details pane if it was collapsed.

features.title: Expiry for secret clips
features.summary: Implemented: secret clips can expire on their own clock, off by default, offered in Settings beside the other secret options and in the wizard's privacy step. A secret past its limit is deleted with its media, and neither pinning it nor filing it in an archive keeps it alive — that is the point of a limit that applies to secrets alone. Ordinary clips are unaffected.

features.title: Blurred secrets keep their ends legible
features.summary: Implemented: a concealed secret shows its first character and its last three, with everything between drawn blurred, so two credentials can be told apart without either being readable. Under eight characters it gives up only its final character, because three of them would be most of the value. Applies to rows, cards and the read-only preview; the editors stay blurred whole, since text under the caret cannot be partly masked.

features.title: Text size for quick preview, remembered
features.summary: Implemented: the preview has its own text size in percent, clamped between 70 and 250, offered from the preview's footer and from Settings and remembered across restarts. It applies to the rendered view, the Markdown source and the editor alike, so switching between them never changes the size.

features.title: Scrolling capture shows no banner
features.summary: A scrolling capture runs for 15 seconds with no visible sign that it is running or that Esc will end it. The toast window is created and positioned correctly — the log from a real run reads `capture banner at 327,1531 (window 21..1523), placed Ok(())` — so the window exists on screen and still shows nothing, which points at the paint path rather than at placement. The banner has to be unmissable: it must paint reliably, and it should not be hidden behind the target window or pushed out of view by a taskbar. `SetWindowDisplayAffinity` with WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE would let it sit over the window being captured without appearing in the captured pixels, which removes the rule that it has to stay outside the target rectangle.

features.title: Escape does not stop a scrolling capture
features.summary: Pressing Esc during a scrolling capture does nothing; the run only stops when the page reaches its end. The loop polls `picker::escape_pressed()`, which reads GetAsyncKeyState behind a low-level keyboard hook that swallows physical keys, at the top of every step and after each settled frame, so the press either never reaches that check or is masked by the blocking hook. Escape has to end the capture promptly, keep the rows captured so far, release the input hooks and close the banner.

features.title: Window capture should be the content only
features.summary: Window and scrolling captures include the window's own chrome: a Chrome window comes back 942x1500 with the tab strip and the address bar in it. Only the content inside the window is wanted. The content area has to be found rather than guessed — UI Automation exposes the document or main pane of a window with a real bounding rectangle — with the client area as the fallback for windows that expose no document, and the window rectangle as the last resort. The same cropping applies to both flows, and the stitched scrolling image must not gain fixed rows it no longer has.

features.title: Shorten the scrolling capture menu label
features.summary: The capture menu item reads "Scroll a window and capture its full length"; it should read "Scroll and capture a window".

features.title: Sidebar filter field touches the header rule
features.summary: The filter box under a sidebar section header sits flush against the rule at the bottom of the header. It needs clear space above it so the two do not touch, in every section that has a filter box (Collections, Archives, Tags, Searches).

features.title: Collapsed sidebar headers have a gap between them

features.title: Opt-in paste back into the foreground app

features.summary: A DPAPI-wrapped data key seals preview, body and file columns with AES-256-GCM under a fresh nonce per record.

features.title: Per-user NSIS installer

features.title: Setting page dynamic search

features.title: Draggable card-size slider

features.title: Configurable clip storage location

features.title: Gear-style settings icon

features.title: Themes with color pickers
features.summary: Dark and light presets plus a custom mode with a swatch and hex field per color token; palettes are applied as CSS custom properties.

features.title: Collection hover actions no longer overlap the count
features.summary: The clip count hides while a collection's hover actions are shown, so archive and delete no longer sit on top of it.

features.title: Archive collections
features.summary: Collections can be archived: their clips leave the history views and search, survive clear-history and retention, and return when unarchived.

features.title: Retention by hours or days
features.summary: The maximum age can be expressed in hours or days, and archived clips are exempt from every retention limit.

features.title: Copy button in list and card views
features.summary: Hovering a row or card reveals a copy button that copies without hiding the window, unlike Enter or double click.

features.title: Search covers tag names
features.summary: Tag names are folded into the in-memory search index, so a clip filed under #invoice turns up for "invoice" even when its body never says the word.

features.title: Confirmation before deleting a collection
features.summary: Deleting a collection opens a confirmation dialog that spells out that the clips themselves are kept.

features.title: Order by dropdown in the history views

features.title: Remove the Enter-copies hint from the status bar
features.summary: The bottom bar no longer claims what Enter does; it keeps the clip count, storage use, encryption state and hotkey.

features.title: Searchable text in screenshots

features.title: Settings toggles stay inside their pill when zoomed
features.summary: The switch knob is centred with flexbox and clipped by the track, so fractional rounding at non-100% interface scales can no longer push it outside.

features.title: Auto-update from GitHub releases
features.summary: A signed in-place updater checks the latest GitHub release once a day (toggleable in settings), shows an install banner, downloads with progress and relaunches; a tag-triggered workflow builds and publishes the signed artefacts.

features.title: Card size resizes live while dragging
features.summary: The grid follows a local scale while the slider moves and the setting is written after the gesture pauses, so thumbnails resize under the pointer.

features.title: Per-category default view
features.summary: Every history category keeps its own list/cards choice, configurable in Appearance; images default to cards and everything else to rows.

features.title: Reveal clips and archives in Explorer

features.title: Always on Top setting preference

features.summary: A payload that is entirely a hex or rgb()/rgba() value is recognised as a color: cards, rows and the preview pane paint the sample with the copied code overlaid, and a dedicated Colors view lists them.

features.title: Pause capture with a private mode
features.summary: A tray menu, a second global hotkey and a settings row pause clipboard capture for 15 minutes, an hour, or until restart; the watcher ignores changes while paused and the status bar shows a resume chip.

features.title: Quick-paste slots with Ctrl+1-9
features.summary: Ctrl+1 through Ctrl+9 copy the matching visible result without moving the selection, auto-pasting when that setting is on; rows and cards show their slot number.

features.title: Auto-clear the clipboard after use
features.summary: Optionally empties the Windows clipboard a configurable time after a copy, or as soon as the overlay hides, and leaves it alone if anything else was copied in the meantime.

features.title: Manage tags from the sidebar

features.title: Tag Filter

features.title: Flag likely API keys and secrets
features.summary: Detect secrets in text at capture time and mark the clip. High-precision rules cover PEM private keys, known token prefixes (GitHub ghp_/github_pat_, Stripe sk_live_, Slack xox*, Google AIza, OpenAI sk-proj-, Anthropic sk-ant-, npm, SendGrid, Twilio, AWS AKIA/ASIA), JWTs, URLs with embedded credentials and authorization headers. Detection runs on plaintext in read_content before encryption and persists only a confidence level in the plaintext bookkeeping columns, so list rendering never decrypts. Previews are blurred with click-to-reveal, and a separate setting can skip capture entirely. Passwords are deliberately out of scope for text matching because they are indistinguishable from product codes, so they stay covered by clipboard opt-out formats and the ignored-apps list. features.title: Capture the full animated GIF when a GIF is copied from a browser
features.summary: Windows has no animated-GIF clipboard format, so a browser's Copy image only ever supplies the frame it is showing. Capture now inspects the CF_HTML fragment that rides along with an image copy for an / GIF (including small data: URLs) and fetches the source asset off the watcher thread. The downloaded animation is stored as .gif beside the still frame, which remains the thumbnail and OCR source. The clip is marked animated, so copy/paste republishes the file through CF_HDROP instead of a bitmap and every frame survives in chat apps and editors. The path is not limited to GIPHY and never touches the GIPHY key or its rate limits. Because arbitrary hosts are allowed it uses a general HTTPS-only fetcher: it resolves and rejects loopback, private, link-local and CGNAT addresses, refuses credentials and non-standard ports, pins redirects to the original host, requires an image/gif content type, keeps the 32 MB cap and request timeout, and sniffs the GIF header before caching. Edge cases: CF_HDROP wins, so copying a real .gif in Explorer already yields the full animation. blob: URLs are skipped, hotlink failures and non-GIF responses fall back silently to the static frame at debug level, and inline data: GIFs are decoded up to a 2 MB ceiling.

features.title: add zoomed color view to the cursor when selecting a color with eyedropper
features.summary: The screen sampler now shows a small topmost magnifier beside the crosshair from the moment the pick starts. The popup follows the cursor across the virtual desktop, flips at monitor edges, never takes focus or intercepts clicks, and disappears when the pick finishes or is cancelled. If it cannot be created the original pick still works.

features.title: The sort dropdown doesn't work to sort clips by various dates.
features.summary: The backend sorting was already correct (covered by store tests), but the history hook only refetched when the filter or query changed. Choosing a new order updated the setting without reloading the list, so nothing moved. The hook now takes the sort order as a dependency, so every selection of Last used ↑/↓ or Captured ↑/↓ immediately refetches and reorders the history.

features.title: Add the filter function to "collections" and limit of 6
features.summary: Collections now behave like Archives and Tags: a filter box matches names as you type (Enter opens the first match, Escape clears), the list shows the configured sidebar limit (6 by default) and offers Show all with a compact scrollable list. The Sidebar lists setting in Appearance controls the shared limit.

features.title: In color preview thumbnail view and properties, show both the HEX and RGB values
features.summary: Colour swatches now render the normalised HEX code and the matching rgb(r, g, b) value together, in the list thumbnail, the grid card and the preview pane. The Details section already listed both and still does; the swatch tooltip repeats them so the values remain available when a tiny thumbnail truncates the second line.

features.title: for the GIF utility add a button to add your custom gif file
features.summary: The GIF utility toolbar has an Add GIF file button that opens a .gif picker. The chosen file is sniffed for the GIF header, capped at 32 MB and copied into the media folder under a content-addressed name, so the shelf entry survives the original being moved or deleted. It appears immediately in Your GIFs and copies through CF_HDROP, preserving every frame. Imported entries are validated when settings load: only bare .gif names inside the media folder are accepted.

features.title: Performance for the Emoji all view is still poor
features.summary: The earlier fixes were present: rows are virtualised and glyphs are pre-rasterised through an idle canvas. The remaining cost came from the virtual window itself and from how the warmer forced rasterisation. features.title: Scrolling screenshot mode
features.summary: Picks a window, brings it forward and parks a real pointer in it, then reads the window from the desktop a wheel notch at a time. Each step waits for the window to change and then to stop changing, so a half-scrolled frame is never stitched in. The distance comes from stitch::scroll_offset, which minimises the mean absolute difference over the frame (a compositing browser re-renders glyphs with sub-pixel differences, so byte matching peaks well below 100% even at the true offset) and leaves out rows and columns that are pinned to the window. Only the new rows are appended, and the columns that belong to the window rather than the page are held at the fold so a fixed sidebar appears once. Stops on a resize, an unmeasurable frame, no movement through all three scroll methods, 200 steps or 20,000 px, and keeps the partial result. Eleven stitching tests cover the matcher, pinned chrome, frozen columns and an end-to-end rebuild. A confirmed real run captured a 2,943 px Chrome page in 15 steps; the banner and Esc, and cropping the capture to the window's content, are followed up in their own cards.

features.title: Encrypt clips marked secret
features.summary: Marking a clip secret encrypts it; unmarking decrypts it back into an ordinary clip. A random 32-byte data key encrypts the rows and the passphrase only wraps that key, so changing the passphrase rewraps 32 bytes instead of re-encrypting the history, and a database copied to another machine opens with the passphrase alone because the salt and the wrapped key travel inside it. Argon2id (64 MiB, 3 passes) stretches the passphrase; AES-256-GCM with a fresh nonce per value seals each readable column — body, preview, files, OCR text, rich text and note — and a fixed check value is what distinguishes a wrong passphrase from a corrupt file. Every read goes through one helper, so a locked vault returns nothing at all rather than a blurred version: search, copy, export, OCR and rich text all see an empty column. Marking without a vault is refused rather than stored in the clear, a restart always comes back locked, and clips read while locked say so. Proven by tests including sealing a clip, closing the database and reopening it as a restart would. Media is covered too: marking an image secret encrypts the full image, its thumbnail and any recovered animation in place, a locked vault serves no pixels and the card shows a lock instead of a broken frame, and unmarking decrypts them back. Sealed rows deliberately do not match a search while the vault is locked: making them searchable would mean keeping their plaintext somewhere, which is the thing the vault exists to prevent. Threat model: protects the database at rest and copies of it against someone without the passphrase. It does not protect a machine that is compromised while the app is running and unlocked, a keylogger, or memory inspection. A fourth pass seals anything that was flagged secret before the vault existed: on creating, unlocking or changing the passphrase, every secret clip whose columns are still plaintext is encrypted in one transaction, and the command reports how many so the interface can say what happened. The pass is idempotent and does nothing while the vault is locked.

features.summary: Region, window, full-screen and scrolling captures now draw their outline in the colour from Settings. The window highlight had its own hard-coded blue; every overlay path now reads the one setting, through a single helper so a new capture mode cannot drift again.

features.title: When clicking Reveal for a secret in list mode, icon should flip to Hide
features.summary: Reveal now toggles instead of being one-way: once a secret is showing, the same control reads Hide and puts the blur back, in both the row/card preview and the properties pane.

features.title: Headers in the properties menu on right should be collapsible
features.summary: The properties pane's sections fold shut from their grip, and the collapsed set is stored in settings so it survives a restart. A chevron in the header shows the state and the grip still drags to reorder.

features.title: Padding of drag handles on left menu's left side is not the same as padding on right
features.summary: The properties pane's section grips now sit at the same inset as the sidebar's, so the two columns line up.

features.title: Image Editor shortcut
features.summary: Settings gained an Image editor command: the program plus any arguments it needs to open a file, with {file} standing for the image's path and the path appended when there is no {file}, so plain mspaint.exe needs nothing typed. With a command set, an Edit pencil appears on a card's top-right hover icons, on the right of a list row next to the copy icon, in the quick image preview's footer, and in the right-click menu. Picking ShotCraft from the dialog fills in open-annotate --filepath, which is the mode its CLI needs. Images sealed in the vault are refused with an explanation rather than handing ciphertext to an editor that would save plaintext back over the seal. The command is a command line, not a bare path: an unquoted program path with spaces is repaired at launch (and reported in full when it is missing), and when the editor finishes CopyPaste rebuilds the clip's thumbnail and pixel size from what was saved and reloads the list, waiting on the editor's process or, for a hand-off to an already-running copy, on the file itself.

features.title: Double clicking archives, tags and collections lets you inline edit them
features.summary: Double-clicking a collection, an archive or a tag turns its name into a field in the sidebar, with the text already selected: Enter or clicking away saves, Esc abandons the change and no longer reaches the window handler that would hide the app. Collections and archives had no rename affordance at all before, so this is now the way they are renamed; the list title follows when the renamed collection is the one on screen, and a tag renamed onto an existing name merges as it always did.

features.title: Add to Archive > New Archive right click option needed
features.summary: The Add to Archive submenu leads with New archive…, mirroring New collection…: it asks for a name, creates the archive and files the clip into it in one step, so a clip can be archived into a fresh archive without leaving the list. The item is there even with no archives yet, which also gives the submenu something to show.

features.title: Error humanize it's wording
features.summary: Renaming a collection or an archive onto a name another one already uses said “database error: UNIQUE constraint failed: collections.name”, because the rename went straight to the UNIQUE index. It is now checked first, case-insensitively like the index, and answered with “a collection or archive named “Work” already exists”. Renaming something to the name it already has is still allowed, whitespace and case aside, since that is not a clash with itself. Creating a collection already explained itself this way; the rename path now matches it.

features.title: Scrolling screencapture tweaks
features.summary: Both problems are fixed. The scroll bar is recognised from the first frame and left out of every frame that follows, so it can no longer repeat down the right edge: a bar is a band of columns painted as one flat track with a single stretch of another colour in it for the thumb, which a page margin (no thumb) and an overlay bar (page showing through) both fail, and the width is measured rather than assumed. Against two real frames left by an earlier failed capture the detector found the 15 px bar and found nothing once it was cropped. The pointer is now parked off the page between steps — on the window's title bar, where the wheel still routes to it — so no link is hovered while frames are read, Chrome draws no URL preview, and the hover state cannot change as the page slides underneath; it returns to where the user left it when the capture ends, whichever way it ends.

features.title: Enhance the Tray Icon with shortcuts
features.summary: The tray menu is a working shortcut surface rather than four entries. Right click offers New clip…, a Capture submenu (Region, Window, Full screen, Scrolling, Colour picker) that runs the same paths the title bar does, and a Pause capture submenu (15 minutes, 1 hour, Until restart). The menu is rebuilt whenever its contents depend on state, so Pause capture gives way to a single “Resume capture (12 min left)” item while a pause runs, and Lock vault appears only while the vault is open — both pushed from the places that change that state, including a timer that fires when a timed pause expires, since nothing else emits an event then. Settings…, Data folder and Quit fill out the rest, and the tooltip carries the pause state. Open CopyPaste and Clear unpinned history left the menu: left click already opens the window, and Clear history lives in Settings → Storage with both variants. Tests cover the pause wording, the rounding to whole minutes, and an expired pause reading as plain paused.

features.title: when clicking "save color palette", play clip sound
features.summary: Saving a color palette now plays the copy sound, so it honours the copy-sound toggle and any WAV chosen in Settings, with the bundled tick as the fallback. The confirmation was already written, but the full-screen preview draws over the notice strip, so the preview now repeats the message inside its own frame; the properties pane keeps using the strip. The message names the archive the colors went into, e.g. “Saved 5 colors to “Color Palette 3”.”

features.title: when deleting a clip, maintain current position on clip board
features.summary: Deleting a clip used to scroll the board back to the top, because the deleted clip took the selection with it and the selection effect then pointed at the first clip. The selection now passes to the clip that takes the deleted one's place — the one after it, or the one before it when the end of the list was removed — and the list keeps its scroll position. Bulk delete does the same, landing on the first clip after the removed block. Both the list and thumbnail views use the same selection, so both are fixed.

features.title: Tray menu quick actions
features.summary: Right-clicking the tray icon offers New clip, a Capture submenu (region, window, full screen, scrolling, colour picker), Pause capture (15 minutes / 1 hour / until restart) that turns into Resume capture while paused, Settings, Data folder, Lock vault while the vault is open, and Quit. The menu and tooltip are rebuilt whenever the pause or vault state changes, a timed pause refreshes itself when it expires, and the one-click Clear unpinned history row and the always-present Resume row are gone.

features.title: Capture short videos in GIF and image cards
features.summary: Copied browser media is kept as the MP4 the page served, stored beside the still frame and played in the app. Detection reads the copied CF_HTML and classifies by query before path, so `…/clip.gif?format=mp4` is a video while the same path without the query stays a GIF; `` src/srcset, `

features.title: When adding a clip to an archive, the page scrolls to the beginning.
features.summary: Filing the selected clip into an archive took it out of the list, so the selection fell back to the first row and the view jumped to the top. The selection now moves first: one shared `selectSurvivor` helper hands it to the clip after the ones leaving (or the one before, at the end of the list), and delete, bulk delete, filing into an archive from the properties pane, and dropping clips onto an archive all use it. Filing into a collection keeps the clips visible, so nothing moves then, and an archive being browsed with the Archives toggle on is left alone for the same reason.

features.title: Generate and store a preview of the link for link clips?
features.summary: Two halves, as proposed. **Offline:** a link clip draws a tile from its own address — the site's initial on a hue derived from the host, with the host underneath on a card — computed in the frontend with no network and nothing stored. **On demand:** the properties pane's image button and a **Load link preview** right-click entry ask the page for its picture; a new `preview` module fetches the page with the movie fetcher's guards (HTTPS only, public hosts, credentials refused, redirects pinned to the page's host), then reads `og:image` → `og:image:url` → `twitter:image` → `rel="image_src"` with a small tag reader that handles quoted, unquoted, single-quoted and mixed-case attributes and decodes the common entities; the image is resolved against the page, fetched with an 8 MB cap, decoded and re-encoded at the 400px thumbnail box, and stored in the clip's `thumb_path` so every existing display, delete and seal path picks it up. A 2 MB page cap, and a body that is not an image is rejected rather than stored. A replaced preview deletes the file it replaced. **Automatic:** `linkPreviewsAuto` (Settings → Capture, **off by default**) fetches the same preview during capture for a clip that is only an https link, skipping clips that already have one. A secret clip's preview is sealed with the rest of its media. Tests cover the tag/entity parser and its fallbacks, relative resolution, address validation, storage and replacement cleanup, and sealed storage refused while the vault is locked.

features.title: Add a quick view for Video Clips
features.summary: Space on a video clip now opens a player instead of the text editor: native transport controls, a scrubbable timeline, the copied still frame as poster, looping playback, and the header reading “Video preview”. Seeking needed more than the element, so the media scheme now answers HTTP range requests — 206 with Content-Range and Accept-Ranges, a single range clamped to the file, `-500` suffixes and open-ended ranges handled, and the whole file returned when the range is unusable. That is what makes the timeline scrub without waiting for the entire clip. A secret clip's video stays blurred and silent with no controls until Reveal.

features.title: Allow video clips to be added to "My GIFs"
features.summary: The save-to-shelf button was hidden behind `kind === image`, so a video clip had no way in. It now appears for any clip carrying a moving asset — a captured video, a copied frame with a recovered video, or a pasted movie address that is still a link clip — and shows a camera rather than a film frame when that asset is a video. The shelf itself already resolved a clip's still and moving sources through `getClip`, so a video files into the hidden Saved GIFs archive and plays in the shelf exactly like a GIF, and copying it from the shelf publishes the MP4.

features.title: Add a new main category of clips called "Media"
features.summary: The sidebar's Images row is now **Media**, with a new media icon, expanding into Images (All) — which carries the image count the group used to show — Screenshots, People, GIFs and Video. GIFs and Video are separate views now rather than one “GIFs & videos” list: the backend gained `gifOnly` (moving asset is a GIF) and `videoOnly` (moving asset is a video) filters, and both cover every clip kind, so a pasted movie address lands under Video and a copied frame with a recovered GIF under GIFs. The group selects Images (All) on click and highlights for any of its four views, and the per-category layout memory treats them as one Media category, so a grid chosen for images stays a grid for video.

features.title: Create a shortcut setting for "New Clip"
features.summary: Settings → Activation gained a **New clip shortcut** row, and the first-run wizard's Activation step offers the same field next to the global hotkey. The field is optional — Backspace clears it, and an empty value means no shortcut — so nothing is claimed on a fresh install. It is registered through the same bindings as everything else, so a malformed combination is reported while you type and a combination already used by the summon key, the pause toggle, a capture shortcut or Print Screen is refused with the owner's name. Pressing it opens the small New clip window, bypassing the summons/paste path entirely; if Windows refuses the key at startup, the optional set falls back so the summon key still works.

features.title: When using the quick image preview, adjust the window size to show all pixels
features.summary: The quick preview now opens at the picture's own size instead of a fixed 980 × 86vh frame: the panel is the image plus its chrome, clamped to 92% of the screen width and 86% of its height. An image too large for the screen opens zoomed out just enough to show all of it — the scale is computed from the panel's width and the image's aspect ratio, and the zoom floor dropped from 50% to 10% so a 4K screenshot fits on a 1080p display — while a small image is never upscaled. The corner grip still resizes the panel afterwards, and a video clip's panel is fitted the same way when its dimensions are known. A later refresh does not resize the window under the user's hands: the fit runs once per preview.

features.title: GIF shelf cards keep their size when the caption is a long link
features.summary: A clip-backed shelf card only set a minimum width, so a long caption — a pasted movie address, for instance — stretched the card across several columns and ignored the Preview size slider, while neighbouring GIFs stayed at their size. The card now has a fixed width from that slider as well, and the caption and its button are told to shrink rather than push, so every shelf card is the same size whatever its title.

features.title: Stop defaulting focus to search bar on window focus
features.summary: Clicking back into the overlay no longer moves the caret into the search field. Focus is only placed there when the window is summoned to be typed into — the tray icon, the global hotkey, or the route change that reveals history — so coming back from the taskbar, the settings window or another app no longer steals the keyboard from wherever the user was.

features.title: When "Always on Top" is set to yes it should apply to all app windows
features.summary: "Always on top" was only applied to the main overlay, so the settings and New clip windows could open behind it. New windows now inherit the preference when they are built, and toggling it walks every open window instead of just the main one, so a settings window already on screen follows the change too. Sticky clip windows stay on top regardless, which is what they are for.

features.title: Make Sticky Feature
features.summary: Right-clicking a clip offers "Make Sticky", which opens it in its own borderless, always-on-top window sized to its content: an image opens at its own dimensions (scaled down only when it would not fit), text opens at the size of its longest line and line count, and a file list at the length of its paths. The window keeps a thin drag header with a close button, can be resized down to 220 × 160, and refreshes itself when the clip changes, such as when the vault is locked or the clip is edited. Opening the same clip again focuses the window already on screen rather than stacking duplicates. Secret text stays masked.

features.title: Sometimes when I take a screenshot or copy, the paste is an older item
features.summary: Two places left an older item on the clipboard. A screenshot taken with the app's capture buttons or Print Screen was only ever stored in the history - the clipboard was never touched - so the next Ctrl+V pasted whatever was copied before it; a completed capture is now written to the clipboard with the watcher's hash armed, exactly like copying an image clip, and the notice says the screenshot is on the clipboard. Separately, Ctrl+C in the overlay did nothing: the webview had no selection of its own, so the native copy left the previous clipboard entry in place, which read as it pasted an old clip. Ctrl+C now copies the clip under the cursor and keeps the overlay open; inside a text field it still copies the text.

features.title: For Sticky Images add some features
features.summary: A sticky image now has a zoom control in the bottom-right corner — minus, the current percentage (a click resets it to 100%), and plus — and the wheel zooms one step per burst, so a trackpad cannot fly through the range. Zoom runs from 25% to 400%, the image keeps its aspect ratio at every step, and the picture scrolls once it is larger than the window. Videos are left alone, since they have their own controls.

features.title: For Sticky notes with text make text selectable
features.summary: Text selection is opt-in across the app, because stray highlights on the chrome read as a bug; the sticky window was not opting in, so nothing in a text note could be selected. The note body is selectable now, which makes copying a line out of a sticky the same drag as anywhere else.

features.title: For sticky notes that are links, make link clickable
features.summary: A sticky note holding a link now opens it: the arrow beside the close button sends the address to the default browser, and a double-click on the address itself does the same. The address stays selectable, so copying it is still one drag, and only clips recognised as links get the affordance.

features.title: For Sticky Videos
features.summary: A sticky video plays as soon as the window opens — muted and looping — and its transport controls appear only while the pointer is over it, so the chrome does not sit on the picture for the life of the window.

features.title: When copying video files, nothing copies
features.summary: A video clip was published as a dropped file only, and plenty of targets refuse that format, so a paste produced nothing. A video whose asset was recovered from an address now puts the file and the original link on the clipboard together: file-aware targets paste the movie, and everything else pastes the link. GIFs keep their previous behaviour, and a video copied as a file still publishes the file alone.

features.title: Quick Preview of Colors
features.summary: Space on a colour clip now opens a dedicated preview: the swatch fills the left at panel height, and the right lists the same colour as HEX, RGB and HSL, each with a copy button that puts that exact notation on the clipboard — so hsl(...) can go straight into a stylesheet. The values are selectable, and a clip marked secret still opens masked.

features.title: Stick images changes
features.summary: The image area of a sticky is a proper zoom stage now: the picture is scaled against the window and dragged with the pointer, instead of sitting in a flex-centred scroller whose overflow was clipped equally on both sides — which is why anything past 100% looked like it did nothing. Zoom moves in 25% steps from 25% to 400%, eases in over 140ms unless Windows asks for reduced motion, and the drag is clamped so the picture cannot be lost; clicking the percentage resets both.

features.title: sticky Markdown files
features.summary: A markdown clip in a sticky now opens rendered, with a Plain/Markdown toggle in the header for the source, matching the quick preview. The body stays selectable; editing and the text-size control stay in the app, since a sticky is a reference surface.

features.title: Sticky Files
features.summary: Every path in a sticky file list has an open button beside it that hands the file to its default application, and the paths are selectable so one can be copied out.

features.title: The quick preview for colors has buttons it doesn't need
features.summary: The colour quick preview no longer shows the text-size control or the Edit button: a colour has no text to resize and nothing worth editing, and the HEX, RGB and HSL rows already carry copy buttons. The sticky window gained the same colour panel - swatch, three notations, three copy buttons - so the two previews agree.

features.title: For image preview of GIFs or PNGS, add a checkered background to indicate it's transparent
features.summary: Previewed pictures now sit on a transparency grid. It is drawn behind the picture box itself — not behind the panel — so it appears only where the pixels are see-through, and an opaque screenshot covers it completely, which means nothing has to detect whether a PNG or GIF has an alpha channel. It follows the theme, and covers both the quick preview and sticky windows, GIFs included.

features.title: copying items from inside copypaste doesn't add it to the history, even though I hear the copy sound
features.summary: Copies made inside the app were written to the clipboard, played the tick and deliberately told the watcher to ignore its own write - so nothing was recorded. That covered the emoji browser, the HEX/RGB/HSL buttons on a colour preview, the colour-scheme copy and a message copied from an error banner. Those copies now insert the text as a clip with the watcher still suppressed, so the entry appears once instead of twice, and the Source column names where it came from: Emoji, Color, Color scheme or CopyPaste. Copying an existing clip is unchanged: it moves to the top without a duplicate. A history that refuses an oversized payload is logged and does not fail a copy that already succeeded.

features.title: Add keyboard navigation to quick previews
features.summary: Implemented: the left and right arrows step through the list while the quick preview is up, showing the previous or next clip and moving the selection with it, so the list can be browsed without closing the overlay. File lists are stepped over because they have no quick preview, and the keys stay with a text field being edited or a video's own seeking. The overlay is keyed by clip, so each step still flushes a pending edit and re-fits the media — but the dimmed, blurred backdrop stays up (the fade and rise only play when the preview opens) and the fit runs before paint, so stepping never flashes the list or snaps the zoom.

features.title: After using an external editor launched from copy/paste the thumbnail doesn't update on saving of the edited image
features.summary: Implemented: the clip is rebuilt on every save, not when the editor closes. While the editor runs, the image file is watched and the thumbnail, pixel size and dimensions follow once a save has settled (the file's stamp reads the same twice in a row, so a half-written PNG is never decoded); further saves in the same session rebuild again. ShotCraft never saves over the file it was given and its open-annotate has no output flag, so for shotcraft.exe the save_dir from %APPDATA%\shotcraft\settings.json is watched as well and the newest image that appears there is adopted — names already in the folder and CopyPaste's own <uuid>.png/.thumb.png files are never taken, the folder is relisted only when its own stamp moves, and ten minutes without a new export ends the watch. The exported file is left where the editor put it.

features.title: Copy text in an image adds a clipboard entry
features.summary: The Copy text button in the properties pane's Text in image section put the recognised text on the clipboard but left the history alone, so the text could not be pinned, tagged or found again once the clipboard moved on. Pressing it now also writes the text into the history as its own text clip, filed with the source "Text in image", and the list refreshes with it at the top while the image still counts as used. A history that refuses the entry only logs a warning, so a good copy never reports a failure.

features.title: When using Google Drive as the storage location streaming errors happen
features.summary: Implemented: a data folder on a streaming drive is no longer asked for the same thumbnail over and over. Thumbnails the window has read are kept in a local cache under the app's cache folder and served from there without touching the history folder; a read that still has to go to the drive is one of at most four in flight, retried twice with a growing pause before it is treated as missing, so a fast scroll cannot outrun the driver or leave gaps in the list. Full-size stills get a 32 MB most-recently-used memory cache, which makes arrow-key stepping between clips cheap. Sealed media is never cached — it is decrypted per request — and the disk cache trims itself to 64 MB at startup, dropping leftover partial writes. Verified on the user's Google Drive folder: nine thumbnails were cached on first launch, and the next launch served all nine from the cache with no rewrite.

features.title: Improve scrolling capture
features.summary: When performing a scrolling capture, there is a multi-second wait at the end before the process finishes, that wait should be much shorter

features.title: Right side property menu should now let the resize
features.summary: Right side property menu should now let the resize go so far as to let the trash icon touch the side of the window, lock the minimize size horizontally when dragging so you can't shrink it too much. Likely just pad the last trash icon by 15-20 pixels on the right side.

features.summary: when right clicking a video, add "Copy Video URL" and "Copy Video File" instead of just Copy

features.title: Screen Recording ability
features.summary: Screen recording: a record toolbar (window, region, fixed-size, full screen) with an audio-source dropdown, pointer toggle, pause/stop controls, blinking outline, start click, hotkeys in a new Screen Recording settings section, and FFmpeg encoding to an MP4 that lands in the history as a video clip (install FFmpeg with one click when missing).
